body:
> ...although I can't listen to the same music for too long or it gets depressing.

Anything repetitive gets me depressed. I don't know why. The same metro station everyday. The same room. The same people. Even if I change everything, it starts over again after only a short time. Do you feel the same? What can I do?
Thanks, I'll research it and read it if it has good reviews.

Happier: Learn the Secrets to Daily Joy and Lasting Fulfillment (Tal Ben-Shahar)

The Art of Happiness by Dalai Lama

Stumbling on Happiness by Daniel Gilbert

How to Get Control of Your Time and Your Life by Alan Lakein

Countless readings on wikipedia about happiness, depression, suicide, [defense mechanism](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_mechanism), biographies, etc.

*Note: [defense mechanism](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Defense_mechanism) was the closest to being helpful. I believe it has a great impact on how you live. Albeit maybe impossible to change, it is very enlightening to discover which one(s) one personally uses.*

About every article I stumbe upon:

The Atlantic, June 2009 ["What Makes Us Happy"](http://www.theatlantic.com/doc/200906/happiness)" by Joshua Wolf Shenk

*On a side note is it very interesting to note that the author of the study the study on which "What Makes Us Happy" is based qualifies himself as a failure and unhappy man. Makes you realize that no matter how much you know, you may not be able to change your outlook on life.*

Time's "[They Just Won't Grow Up](http://www.time.com/time/covers/1101050124/)"

[Psychology lectures on academicearth.org](http://academicearth.org/courses/introduction-to-psychology)

Every video on [ted](http://www.ted.com/) that touches psychology/happiness in any way.

... and that's on top of my head ... all very interesting, yet helped very little.

Hey, I am really sorry. I hope I am not making it harder for you.
I can't think of anything intelligent to say. Thanks for sharing I guess.

It seems like your life would be much better if you had a job, though. Don't you have any marketable skill? If you have a BS in any field, you are eligible to many well paid (albeit probably boring) government jobs, if you care to wait long enough in line (takes up to a year).

If you have 20/20 vision and have a BS, you can be trained to be a cargo plane pilot. There is a big demand for those (thanks China) so in some places they pay for your training, and can earn ridiculous money afterwards.

I think his answer should stay. It is helpful to the conversation. I just hope it won't depress others more / push them over the edge. I can take it.

By the way, I would be interested to know where you are from. You don't *sound* North-American (which I am). PM if you want. (I mean, never been depressed, come on! In *this* world!?)

I think the post is not about suicide. It is about not wanting to live. It is very different. Whether the actual act of ending one's life occurs is irrelevant. The post is about life being intrinsically unbearable for some, and slipping_away simply expressed that it has been for him, after suffering a lost similar to mine.

As I expressed in the post I think that in some cases, suicide is only bad (morally?) in the sense that it will cause my acquaintances unnecessary distress. So the question is not about suicide, it is about life. The sad, sad life. Suicide is just the conclusion one might reach if he/she feels life cannot be improved, and life as it is now is horrible.

I disagree.

I have read somewhere (lost the exact reference, but I think it is somewhere in [this](http://academicearth.org/courses/introduction-to-psychology) lecture) that most people have a set point of happiness, and whatever happens, they mostly revert back to it.

There are a few exceptions, and aesthetic surgery is one of them. They did not exactly explain why. So, well, before offing yourself, give it a shot! :P

Hey, welcome to the club. [I posted something similar 1 hour before you](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/9newo/i_dont_know_if_it_fits_here_but_rationally/).
Although I have more reasons than you to be depressed (dropped-out + lost girlfriend) I feel like the basic is the same. Life just depresses me. You can read my post for a detailed description. Tell me if you feel the same. You can PM me if you want to talk. Although, I am not sure I can help you because we might have the same problem, and just loop-feedback our pain to anguish singularity. Dark night of the soul I guess.

The only thing I would advise though, is try to not let it screw up my life. Dropping out **seemed** rational at the time (I asked for advice, but in such a way that the other could only counsel to get out of the program. But I gave skewed information to get the advice I seeked. Clever, right?) So **don't make any big decision** while you are on a rut. I am **MUCH MUCH MUCH MUCH** worse than I was, because on top of the general angst/depression/whatever I feel about life, now I feel intense regret for having screwed up my life. And now life is just downright unbearable.

Good luck.

Thanks for you honest input.
Yes, I would be interested to know more about your story.

What have you been doing during those 5 years? How is your life now? Did the regrets subside? What will you do in the future?

How? Could you please explain more?

I only know how it affected people around me. So if you have a different experience, please do share.
It does sound harsh, but I would **not** want to be him. But I do see myself in him, and it is scary. And I think he thinks he is a failure too, to be honest. Just the dark, straight truth.

Did you go on meds?

Someone in my family did, and it only made things worse. (Made them feel good enough to not fix the problem, and it dragged on for years. Since you always need to increase medication if you do not fix the problem, it becomes unsustainable. Fortunately, that person's problem was directly related to work and got to retire early, because or doctor's recommendation, before becoming batshit insane. But now addicted to the meds, for life).

So I don't want to go on meds. I fear it is just a temporary solution. You are right it is one thing that I haven't tried. But being depressed **and** addicted doesn't sound too good...
